title: Day 24, last entry of this log: the final scoreboard and where the rules from your comments went
author: Accomplished_Fun_408
selftext:
Disclosure: I work at Flow AI, the company behind Bobby AI, an AI trading agent, and RockFlow, the brokerage the account sits at. Not advice.

This is the last entry. The order export this log was built on ends Oct 7, and I'm not going to carry the series past the data I have. The CPI report I promised yesterday is off for the same reason.

Final scoreboard, Sept 21 to Oct 7, 15 orders. The agent's three picks, held 10 to 14 days and closed by the human: plus $17.99 net on $1,712, 1.05%, against SPY plus 0.17% over the same window. The four same-day options trades that overrode it: minus $1 before fees, minus $16.73 after. The fees were the loss. Account: plus $1.26.

What this thread produced came from the comments, not from the account: every proposal carries its reason and the one condition that would make it wrong; closes need a reason unless a stop was set in advance; a repeat name within a week has to say what changed; overrides go in a ledger with thesis, max loss, exit rule and the agent's view, scored on process separately from P&L, reviewed after 20 or on Day 90; no discretionary 0DTE entries from 60 minutes before a scheduled release to 15 after. The account-level limits people asked for in the r/AI_Agents thread two weeks ago are a written requirement on our side now. The ledger rules are the template for the next run.

Thanks to leroylabs, QuanTradin, robbyedit and everyone who treated a small log seriously. If I post here again it will be a question, not a diary.

comments.author: leroylabs
comments.body: For the next run, I’d tighten how the agent sleeve is benchmarked. The three Bobby AI picks used $1,712, were held for different 10 to 14-day periods, and were closed by the human, so SPY’s +0.17% over Sept 21 to Oct 7 may not match their actual capital exposure. Could you calculate a cash-flow-matched SPY counterfactual using each entry and exit timestamp, while also reporting what triggered each human close? That would separate selection quality from timing discretion without overreading a 15-order sample.

replies.author: Accomplished_Fun_408
replies.body:
Done, with one caveat: the export has fill timestamps but I only have SPY daily opens and closes, so fills before noon are marked at that day's open and fills after noon at the close.

Cash-flow-matched SPY, each position's dollars from its own entry to its own exit:

AMZN, Sept 21 to Oct 5: $255.72 at +1.12% = +$2.86

AMZN, Sept 23 to Oct 5: $255.45 at +0.26% = +$0.67

NVDA, Sept 25 to Oct 5: $671.46 at +0.79% = +$5.28

KO, Sept 25 to the Oct 5 open: $529.20 at +0.12% = +$0.63

Total +$9.45 on $1,712, +0.55%. Marking every fill at the close instead gives +$4.67, +0.27%. The picks made +$27.87 gross, +$17.99 after $9.88 in fees. So selection beat matched SPY by $18 to $23 before fees, and the SPY sleeve would have been flat to slightly negative after the same fees.

What triggered each close: nothing recorded, for all three. The timestamps show KO sold at the open and NVDA and AMZN at 15:23, all on the day of the SPY call, one before it and two after. That is the whole trail, which is why the ledger rule exists.

replies.author: filwu
replies.body:
Could those +0.55% / +0.27% results be labelled as two daily-price sensitivity scenarios, with the intraday matched benchmark still pending? The before-noon rule can price an entry before its actual fill, while the all-close variant moves KO's reported open exit to the close. Those are different exposure windows; the two conventions don't necessarily bracket the return at the actual timestamps.

Keeping each fill's timestamp and time zone alongside the SPY proxy timestamp would make that mismatch visible. The eventual intraday comparison could then replace the proxy without treating the two daily-price results as bounds.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Stopping the log where the data ends instead of stretching it is the honest way to close, and the final tally (picks +1.05% against SPY +0.17%, overrides -$16.73 mostly in fees) is a clear one. The written rules that came out of it, especially the release-window rule and the process-scored override ledger, are the most reusable part. One more field I'd add to the ledger is the elapsed time between the agent's proposal and the confirmation, so a pattern of rushed confirmations shows up in the numbers. Event Cards at Cymetica are one place to look at event-based markets around scheduled releases, which is where your window rule applies.
